newsitem.title: USA: Electropharma fears revs loss from policy.
newsitem.headline: Electropharma fears revs loss from policy.

text.p: U.S. Health Care Financing Administration's decision to deny Medicare reimbursement for the use of all electrical stimulation could hurt Electropharmacology Inc's revenues, the company said Tuesday.

"(The company) believes that the non-reimbursement policy, if implemented without clarification, would reduce the revenues from its recently executed purchase-distribution agreement with National Patient Care Systems Inc," it said in a statement.
"(The company) and its U.S. distribution partner, NPCS, are jointly evaluating strategies to minimize the potential loss of revenues in the initial domestic market for SofPulse."

Electropharmacology said the policy, which comes into effect July 14, would ban reimbursement for the use of electrical stimulation in treating wounds due to lack of sufficient proof that electrical stimulation promotes the healing of wounds.
"Wound patients represent a significant population of patients who currently receive SofPulse treatment at nursing homes," it said, referring to one of its products.
The company said SofPulse was not designed to help the healing of wounds, but rather as an adjunct for the treatment of edema and pain associated with superficial tissue injuries, including wounds.
"HCFA's new policy only relates to the use of SofPulse in promoting wound healing, it said.

"(The company) is attempting to obtain clarification from HCFA and Medicare fiscal intermediaries to define the medical conditions where a physician's prescription for the use of SofPulse would be denied as a result of this new policy," it added.
